gen-gf-ubuntu-sans-mono-fs-be-vietnam-pr: Steady pen pressure runs through every Ubuntu Sans Mono letter, gaps distinct in c, e and s. Be Vietnam Pro follows in a sans with curve endings held well apart and a high mean line, so a long page feels tidy and unhurried.
gen-gf-underdog-fs-roundo: Expressive from the first glance, Underdog bends its curves without any weight shift. Roundo does the quieter work in sans-serif, keeping small counters open and its n built with arch and stem matching.
gen-gf-underdog-gf-noto-znamenny-musical: That wide horseshoe c is Underdog's calling card, drawn with one fixed nib width throughout. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation sits beside it in sans-serif, its terminals stopping far from the stem, so the page gets a loud voice and a modern, clean one.
gen-gf-unica-one-fs-ranade: Commanding and a bit showy, Unica One draws every stroke at one thickness. Ranade moves in a restrained thick-thin play like a worn wooden stamp, its widely spaced sans-serif line giving the heading's rigid strokes something organic to lean on.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Unica One's very large lowercase eye gives it away at once, with visible daylight in every curve. Noto Sans Buginese feels modern beside it, a plain sans whose open letter mouths and short ascenders loosen the heading's rigid strokes.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation is a clean, modern plain sans with terminals stopping far from the stem, set against Unkempt's flat, unvarying line weight. Their difference is the point.
gen-gf-unlock-fs-paquito: Bold, spaced-out and a little pinched at the joins. Unlock keeps its stems just thicker than the connecting strokes, while Paquito, a classic serif with caps nearly matching its x-height, feels confident, approachable and easy company in small doses.
gen-gf-victor-mono-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Victor Mono marks out its bold, open-tracked letters like chalk across a slate, terminals cut so the counters flow outward. Be Vietnam Pro, a plain sans with curve endings kept well apart, brings the strength of a bent steel rod.
gen-gf-victor-mono-fs-ranade: Chalk-on-slate tracking, bold letters, one pen width. Victor Mono holds that line throughout, and Ranade joins in sans-serif with sturdy hairlines and slightly shifting weight, giving the monospace precision a more organic neighbor.
gen-gf-victor-mono-montserrat: Chalk-slate spacing and bold, open terminals. Victor Mono excels at crisp technical precision with no thick or thin strokes, while Montserrat, in sans-serif, glides smoothly with oversized e and a counters and generous white space.
